label: Bible Study
prompt: Abide in me, and I in you. As the _____ cannot bear fruit of itself, except it abide in the vine; no more can ye, except ye abide in me.
verse: Abide in me, and I in you. As the branch cannot bear fruit of itself, except it abide in the vine; no more can ye, except ye abide in me.
note: A branch doesn't strain to grow grapes — it just stays connected to the vine.

label: Warm-Up Word
prompt: Having many things to write unto you, I would not write with paper and _____: but I trust to come unto you, and speak face to face, that our joy may be full.
verse: Having many things to write unto you, I would not write with paper and ink: but I trust to come unto you, and speak face to face, that our joy may be full.
note: John would rather visit than write — paper and ink can't beat a face-to-face conversation.

label: Sunday School
prompt: When I saw among the spoils a goodly Babylonish _____, and two hundred shekels of silver, and a wedge of gold of fifty shekels weight, then I coveted them, and took them; and, behold, they are hid in the earth in the midst of my tent, and the silver under it.
verse: When I saw among the spoils a goodly Babylonish garment, and two hundred shekels of silver, and a wedge of gold of fifty shekels weight, then I coveted them, and took them; and, behold, they are hid in the earth in the midst of my tent, and the silver under it.
note: Achan's confession: a goodly Babylonish garment, some silver, a wedge of gold — 'I coveted them, and took them.'

label: Deep Water
prompt: O LORD, I know that the way of man is not in himself: it is not in man that walketh to direct his _____.
verse: O LORD, I know that the way of man is not in himself: it is not in man that walketh to direct his steps.
note: Jeremiah admits human beings can't steer their own lives — then asks God to correct him gently.

label: Don't Play With Me
prompt: And my people are bent to _____ from me: though they called them to the most High, none at all would exalt him.
verse: And my people are bent to backsliding from me: though they called them to the most High, none at all would exalt him.
note: 'My people are bent to backsliding from me' — and in the very next verse God cries, 'How shall I give thee up?'
